correctness.rationale: For enemy penalties −N, a player in a coalition containing an enemy has utility at most s−2−N<0; hence individually rational positive-product partitions are enemy-independent and contribute ∏(s_i−1)^{s_i}. Complete cross-part hostility forces separate A,B coalitions, and merging friendly B components strictly improves the product. In A the largest independent class has size a−t; for t=1 the positive-product no-singleton condition sharpens to a−2. The convex function h(s)=s log(s−1) on s≥2, extended by zero on [0,2], and vector majorization by (L,a−L) yield the global bound. A matching transversal realizes (a−t,t) for t≥2, (a−2,2) for t=1. Counting endpoint selections with equal-class quotient gives exact M_t. P1=P2 algebraically and remaining monotonicity follows from strict convexity in the feasible range; fixed-t asymptotic Nash PRODUCT ratios use powers (1−c/(a−1))^{a−d}. Independent unrestricted partition enumeration matched all specified small cases; infinite proof relies on convexity and explicit attainability.
residual_risks: The strict-shape uniqueness at the smallest even equal-size cases requires quotienting unordered coalitions; the proof counts the quotient and independent finite checks reproduce it.

value.rationale: This is an exact all-parameter optimization and optimizer-multiplicity classification for a natural perturbation of complete bipartite hostility: one internal enemy edge creates a third coalition, and a second does not decrease the Nash product despite changing the optimum multiplicity. The plateau and strict subsequent decline quantify a structurally meaningful robustness boundary, beyond positive feasibility or complexity.
residual_risks: Applies to a stylized symmetric −N enemy penalty; conclusions do not extend to weaker or asymmetric disutilities.

limitations: Full Pagano–Schlenga primary paper inaccessible; novelty is best-of-knowledge, not a certificate of priority.
Only symmetric aversion-to-enemies with a matching perturbation on one shore; Nash stability and other graph families not claimed.
